title: Quantization Profile Acceptance Thresholds (Performance + Quality)
author: Jonas Weber
body:
## Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference’s *company-wide acceptance thresholds* for publishing a quantization profile into the Quantization Profile Library.

These thresholds are designed to ensure that published profiles:
- Deliver meaningful cost and/or throughput improvements
- Preserve customer-defined quality expectations (including structured output/tool-calling reliability)
- Remain operationally safe to roll out via route-scoped canaries and fast rollback

This standard applies to **Hosted**, **Dedicated**, and **Private** distribution of Redwood-published profiles.

---
## Scope
**In scope**
- Text generation / chat models (streaming and non-streaming)
- Reranking and embedding models (where quantization is supported by the runtime)
- Profiles targeting fp16/bf16 baselines and quantized variants (int8/int4, weight-only or activation-aware where applicable)

**Out of scope**
- Arbitrary customer-supplied profiles (v1 library is Redwood-published only)
- Experimental one-off internal kernels without production support commitments

---
## Definitions
**Baseline:** The default non-quantized serving path for a model/version on a given GPU class (typically bf16/fp16).

**Profile:** A versioned, signed artifact that describes quantization settings + constraints (kernel family, GPU arch constraints, calibration notes) and is resolved by runtime + routing per request.

**Workload classes**
- **Interactive:** user-facing chat or tool-calling routes with tight tail-latency requirements
- **Batch:** offline summarization, enrichment, analysis jobs where throughput/$ dominates and latency constraints are looser

**Primary metrics**
- **Unit cost improvement:** reduction in *cost per 1K output tokens* (Hosted) and/or *GPU-seconds per 1K tokens* (Dedicated/Private normalized)
- **Throughput improvement:** increase in *output tokens/sec* at matched quality settings
- **Latency regression:** increase in p50/p95 end-to-end latency for the same request shape
- **Quality regression:** delta vs baseline on Redwood’s eval harness prompt sets, plus structured-output reliability metrics

---
## Acceptance requirements (must-pass)
A profile may be *published* only if it meets **all** applicable requirements below.

### 1) Performance improvement thresholds
Performance thresholds are evaluated on the **supported hardware matrix** declared by the profile (e.g., H100-SXM, A100-80GB) and on the request-shape bins defined in the perf plan.

#### 1.1 Minimum improvement to publish
At least one of the following must be met *without violating quality thresholds*:

| Profile type | Minimum unit cost improvement (preferred) | Minimum throughput improvement (alternative) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| int8 (production) | ≥ 15% lower cost per 1K output tokens | ≥ 20% higher output tok/sec | Intended for broad compatibility and conservative quality risk |
| int4 (production) | ≥ 30% lower cost per 1K output tokens | ≥ 35% higher output tok/sec | Higher risk; requires stricter coverage + structured-output gates |
| “experimental” tag | ≥ 10% lower cost OR ≥ 15% higher throughput | — | Only with exception process; see “Exceptions” |

**How “unit cost” is computed**
- Hosted: based on measured GPU time + allocator overheads mapped to internal cost model; reported as “$ / 1K output tokens” and “tokens / $”.
- Dedicated/Private: reported as “GPU-seconds / 1K total tokens” and “output tok/sec per GPU”.

#### 1.2 Latency guardrails
Latency is evaluated end-to-end (gateway + routing + runtime + streaming overhead where applicable) under representative load.

| Workload class | p50 latency | p95 latency | Additional notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Interactive (chat/tooling) | No more than +3% regression | No more than +5% regression | If throughput improves but p95 regresses >5%, profile is rejected or must be route-limited to batch-only |
| Batch | No more than +10% regression | No more than +15% regression | Batch is primarily gated on cost/throughput and error rate |

**Hard fail:** Any profile that increases 5xx rates or timeout rates beyond the error thresholds in Section 3 is rejected regardless of performance gains.

#### 1.3 Long-context performance constraints
For long-context bins (e.g., prompt ≥ 8K tokens or model max-context regimes):
- p95 latency regression must be ≤ +8% (interactive) or ≤ +18% (batch)
- No sustained throughput collapse (defined as ≥ 10% worse output tok/sec than baseline) is allowed

Rationale: long-context issues are disproportionately customer-visible and historically correlated with kernel selection edge cases.

---
### 2) Quality thresholds
Quality is measured using Redwood’s eval harness comparing baseline vs quantized variant on the same model version, prompt sets, and decoding settings.

#### 2.1 Aggregate quality regression limits
A profile must meet **all**:
- **Overall quality regression:** ≤ 0.5% absolute drop on the aggregate suite score (or equivalent composite metric defined by the model family evaluation plan)
- **No critical prompt set regression:** ≤ 2.0% absolute drop on any prompt set labeled *critical* for the model family
- **No safety-critical regression:** must not materially degrade safety classifiers or refusal behavior beyond established safety guardrails (see Applied ML gate doc)

Notes:
- “Critical” prompt sets include long-context, tool-calling / JSON mode (if supported), and high-impact customer archetypes (summarization, extraction).
- If multiple metrics exist (e.g., exact match + rubric score), the strictest gate applies.

#### 2.2 Structured output / tool-calling reliability
For models and routes that support structured outputs (JSON mode, function/tool calling, schema-constrained decoding):

| Metric | Baseline requirement | Allowed regression | Hard floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JSON validity rate | Measure baseline | ≤ 0.3% absolute | ≥ 99.5% |
| Tool call argument parse success | Measure baseline | ≤ 0.5% absolute | ≥ 99.0% |
| Schema conformance (if enforced) | Measure baseline | ≤ 0.5% absolute | ≥ 98.5% |

**Hard fail:** Any increase in “hallucinated tool calls” (tool call emitted when not required) that exceeds +0.2% absolute compared to baseline on the tool-calling prompt set.

Rationale: small structured-output regressions cause outsized application breakage and support load.

#### 2.3 Statistical confidence and sample size
To reduce false approvals:
- Quality comparisons must report 95% confidence intervals (bootstrap or paired test as appropriate).
- A profile may be approved only if the measured regression *and* its upper confidence bound meet the thresholds above.
- Minimum sample size for any gating prompt set: **≥ 250 items** (or a justified alternative with reviewer sign-off).

---
### 3) Reliability and operational safety thresholds
#### 3.1 Error rate limits
Under load conditions defined by the perf suite:
- 5xx rate: must not increase by more than **+0.05% absolute** vs baseline
- Timeout rate: must not increase by more than **+0.02% absolute** vs baseline
- OOM / CUDA failure rate: must not increase by more than **+0.01% absolute** vs baseline

Any regression beyond these limits is a hard fail.

#### 3.2 Fallback behavior required
Profiles must support safe fallback:
- Runtime must detect incompatibility (GPU arch mismatch, kernel constraints, unsupported sequence length regimes) and fall back to baseline without request failure.
- Telemetry must tag execution mode (baseline vs quantized) and profile id/version for dashboards and incident triage.

---
## Evaluation matrix (what must be tested)
A profile is only accepted for the exact scope it has been validated on.

Minimum coverage for publish:
- **Hardware:** every GPU SKU/arch listed in the profile’s scope
- **Sequence length bins:** at minimum (short, medium, long-context) as defined in the perf plan for that model family
- **Decoding modes:** greedy + typical production sampling settings; include streaming if route supports streaming
- **Structured outputs:** required if model/route supports JSON mode or tool-calling

If any required dimension is missing, the profile may be published only with a reduced scope (remove unsupported GPU SKUs/bins) or via the exception process.

---
## Acceptance workflow (summary)
1. **Profile build + metadata** created by Applied ML / Runtime, including constraints and calibration notes.
2. **Perf suite run** produces standardized report (tokens/sec, latency, error rates) segmented by GPU and request-shape bins.
3. **Eval harness run** compares baseline vs quantized with confidence intervals and structured-output checks.
4. **Review + approval** against this standard:
   - Applied ML approves quality gates (owner: Applied ML sponsor)
   - Runtime approves compatibility and operational safety (owner: Serving Runtime lead)
   - SRE reviews rollout safety if any special constraints (owner: SRE lead)
5. **Publish** (signed artifact) and mark as `production` or `experimental`.

---
## Exceptions and waivers
Exceptions exist to support early beta learning while protecting production stability.

### When exceptions are allowed
A waiver may be considered when:
- Performance improvement is material for a key customer archetype but one threshold is narrowly missed, *and*
- The impact can be constrained using route-level controls (batch-only, limited orgs, low canary %), *and*
- Monitoring + rollback automation is in place for the target routes.

Exceptions are **not** allowed for:
- Any security integrity requirement (signing/verification)
- Any hard-fail reliability threshold (Section 3.1)
- Any structured-output hard floors (Section 2.2)

### Exception tiers
| Tier | Tag | Allowed deviation | Additional constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 (limited beta) | experimental | Up to 1.0% aggregate quality regression OR up to +8% p95 interactive latency | Must be opt-in; canary ≤ 5%; auto-disable on regression signal; explicit customer comms |
| E2 (customer-specific) | experimental + customer-scoped | Can exceed E1 only with explicit written customer approval | Must be restricted to named customer org; SRE on-call aware; rollback runbook rehearsed |

### Approval requirements for exceptions
All exceptions require written approval (comment in publish PR) from:
- **Applied ML sponsor:** Dr. Maya Srinivasan (or delegate)
- **Runtime lead:** Mateo Alvarez (or delegate)
- **Reliability sponsor:** Neha Kapoor (or delegate)
- **Product lead (Optimize):** Aditya Rao (for external-facing beta/GA readiness)

Waivers must include:
- Exact threshold(s) waived and measured deltas
- Risk assessment and mitigations (route constraints, monitoring, rollback)
- Expiration date (default: **30 days**) and re-evaluation plan

---
## Documentation requirements (publish checklist)
A profile cannot be marked `production` unless the following are attached to the publish record:
- Perf report link and summary (including GPU matrix + request-shape bins)
- Eval harness report link with confidence intervals
- Structured output reliability results (if applicable)
- Declared hardware + kernel constraints and known limitations
- Rollout recommendation (interactive vs batch suitability, suggested canary progression)

---
## Change management
Updates to this standard require:
- Review from Applied ML, Serving Runtime, SRE, and Product
- Backward compatibility considerations for already-published profiles

Any change that relaxes thresholds must include incident/risk review and a plan for monitoring increased risk.

---
## FAQ
**Q: A profile improves cost a lot, but slightly worsens p95 latency. Can we still publish?**
A: For interactive workloads, p95 regression must be ≤ +5% unless an exception is approved and the profile is restricted (e.g., batch-only routes). For batch workloads, higher latency regressions are allowed within Section 1.2.

**Q: What if quality regression appears only on one customer-specific prompt style?**
A: Do not publish as `production`. Either (a) tighten scope (exclude that workload type), (b) require route-level opt-in and mark as `experimental`, or (c) create a separate profile calibrated for that regime.

**Q: Can we publish for one GPU class while failing another?**
A: Yes—profiles are hardware-scoped. Remove the failing GPU SKU/arch from the scope and publish only for validated hardware.
